decisions.reason: The polymer concrete housing has its own page and fits the core drainage portfolio, so keeping it costs little while its value is still uncertain.
Floor-level shower drainage is central to the firm's strategic direction and holding the option open is cheap, though it is only mentioned on the website so far.
As the flagship design product with its own page, it aligns with the firm's design-focused direction and merits further commitment.
The sloped shower element supports the accessible, low-profile direction, and it is too early for its results to justify abandoning it.
The backflow basement drain has a dedicated page and a specific development announcement, signalling active commitment with promising prospects.
The air-admittance valve is a low-cost complementary accessory that rounds out the system offering, so the option is worth keeping despite its peripheral status.
